q: 1. The construction of a temporary structure required to support an unsafe structure, is called
explain: Shoring is the provision of temporary supports (shores) to prevent the collapse of an unsafe wall or structure during repairs or nearby excavation.

q: 2. A brick which is half as wide as a full brick, is called
explain: A queen closer is created by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves. It is used to maintain the bond (overlap) at the end of a wall course.

q: 3. The heading bond is usually used for
explain: A header bond (bricks laid with ends facing out) is used for walls with a thickness of one full brick (roughly 200mm) to provide better transverse strength.

q: 4. The exterior corner of wall is known as ...........
explain: In masonry, the external corner of a building or the stones/bricks forming that corner are called quoins.

q: 5. Brick wall could fail due to
options: rupture along a vertical joint in poorly bonded walls
explain: Brick walls can fail through various mechanisms including compression (crushing), shear, or poor interlocking (bond) between bricks.

q: 6. In random rubble masonry ...........
options: the stones are neatly dressed and laid in courses
the stones are neatly dressed but not built to courses
the stone are either not dressed or roughly dressed and may be coursed or uncoursed
the stones are not dressed and are laid without mortar
explain: Random rubble masonry uses stones of irregular shapes and sizes, which are roughly dressed or not dressed at all, and can be laid in layers (coursed) or at random.

q: 7. The main purpose of cavity wall is
explain: Cavity walls utilize an air gap to prevent moisture travel, provide thermal resistance, and act as a sound barrier.

q: 8. Cavity wall provided with
explain: The defining feature of a cavity wall is the continuous air space (gap) between the inner and outer leaves.

q: 9. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brick masonry and is used for structures subjected to heavy loads.

q: 10. The bond which consists of alternate courses of headers and stretchers is known as ..........
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond, consisting of one course of headers followed by one course of stretchers.

q: 11. The bond in which the bonding bricks are at an inclination to the direction of the wall is known as...
explain: Raking bonds (like herring-bone or diagonal bond) place bricks at an angle to the wall's face to improve longitudinal strength.

q: 12. A brick masonry could fail due to ..........
options: rupture along a vertical joint in poorly bonded walls
explain: Brick walls can fail through crushing under heavy loads, sliding (shearing) between bricks, or splitting along vertical joints (rupture).

q: 13. Good bonding in the brick masonry is ensured when ..........
options: all bricks used are of uniform size
the vertical joints in alternate courses are in plumb from top to base
bats are used as sparingly as possible
explain: Strength in masonry comes from uniform materials, vertical alignment of joints (plumb), and minimizing the use of broken bricks (bats).

q: 14. Minimum width of load bearing wall should be
explain: A standard load-bearing brick wall is usually at least one full brick thick (roughly 230mm including plaster).

q: 15. A wall which is constructed to divide the space within the building into rooms is called ..........
explain: Partition walls are non-load-bearing internal walls used to create separate rooms within a structure.

q: 16. Brick lintels are used when the span is ..........
explain: Brick lintels are weak in tension and are only suitable for small openings, typically less than 1 meter.

q: 17. The wedge shaped units of masonry forming an arch are called ..........
explain: Voussoirs are the individual wedge-shaped blocks (stones or bricks) that make up the body of an arch.

q: 18. A row of arches in continuation is called ..........
explain: An arcade is a succession of arches, each spanning an opening and supported by columns or piers.

q: 19. A junction at which two walls meet at an angle other than 90° is called
explain: A squint junction occurs when walls meet at an acute or obtuse angle, requiring special 'squint' bricks.

q: 20. The points from which the curve of arch springs at the supports are called ..........
explain: Springing points are the specific points where the arch begins to curve away from the support.

q: 21. The rise of the arch is defined as the clear vertical distance between ..........
options: the springing line and the highest point on extrados
the springing line and the highest point on intrados
the center of the arch and the crown of the arch
explain: Rise is measured vertically from the horizontal line connecting the springing points (springing line) to the highest point of the intrados.

q: 22. The pointed arch in which the depth is more at the crown than at the springing is known as ..........
explain: In a variable depth arch, the thickness of the arch rings changes throughout its span, usually being thicker at the crown.

q: 23. If the center of the arch lies below the springing line, it is ..........
explain: A segmental arch is less than a semi-circle, meaning its center point is located below the springing line.

q: 24. The angle of the skew-back with the horizontal in the case of flat arches is usually ..........
explain: For flat arches, the skewback is typically cut at a 60-degree angle to the horizontal to create a stable base for the compression units.

q: 25. The live load on the floors of residential buildings, hospital wards, private sitting room in hostels should be
explain: The standard design live load for residential areas and private rooms is 2.0 kN/m² (approx 200 Kg/m²).

q: 26. Brick lintels are used when the span is
explain: Plain brick lintels have very low tensile strength and are restricted to spans of 1 meter or less.

q: 27. Normally the rise of the steps would be
explain: A riser height of 10cm to 15cm is standard for comfortable climbing, especially in public infrastructure.

q: 28. A facing and shelf, usually ornamental above the fire place is called ..........
explain: A mantelpiece is the decorative frame around a fireplace that often includes a shelf above it.

q: 29. The bricks used for face work shall be ..........
explain: First-class bricks are used for face work because they have uniform color, sharp edges, and a smooth texture, providing a better aesthetic finish.

q: 30. The brick laid with its length parallel to the face of the wall is called a ..........
explain: A stretcher is a brick laid so that its long face is parallel to the face of the wall.

q: 31. Frog is defined as a ..........
options: depression on the top face of a brick
brick whose one end is cut splayed or mitred for the full width
brick used for the corner of a wall
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top face of a brick designed to hold mortar and create a mechanical key between courses.

q: 32. The most important purpose of a frog in a brick is to ..........
options: form keyed joint between brick and mortar
explain: By filling with mortar, the frog creates a strong 'key' that prevents the bricks from sliding relative to one another.

q: 33. A course of stone masonry provided immediately above the cornice, is called ..........
explain: A blocking course is a heavy course of stone laid over the cornice to add weight and stabilize the structure.

q: 34. In the first class coursed rubble masonry ..........
options: all the courses are of the same height
minimum height of the course is limit to 150 mm
the length of the quoin is generally kept 450 mm
explain: First-class coursed rubble requires uniform course heights and specific stone dimensions for maximum structural integrity.

q: 35. A bond consisting of heading and stretching courses so arranged that one heading course comes after several stretching courses, is called ..........
explain: Facing bond is used when expensive facing bricks are used for the outer skin and cheaper bricks for the backing.

q: 36. The arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond in ..........
explain: Dutch bond is a modified version of English bond that uses specialized patterns at the corners to avoid using too many closers.

q: 37. A retaining wall is commonly required in the construction of ..........
explain: Retaining walls are essential whenever there is a need to maintain a difference in ground surface elevation, common in hill roads, dam abutments, and bridge wing walls.

q: 38. In constructing concrete partition wall, the concrete mixture usually adopted is ..........
explain: M150 (approx. 1:2:4) is standard for non-structural or lightly loaded concrete partitions.

q: 39. The surface of the abutment on which the arch rests, is known as ..........
explain: The skewback is the inclined or splayed surface of an abutment prepared to receive the arch.

q: 40. In a flat arch, the skew back is made to rest in an inclined position so as to make an angle of .......... with the springing line.
explain: In flat arches, the skewback usually makes a 60-degree angle to provide sufficient lateral thrust for stability.

q: 41. The lower portion of an arch between the skew back and crown is called ..........
explain: The haunch is the lower half of the arch, between the crown and the skewback.

q: 42. The vertical distance between the wall plate and top of the ridge is called .......... of roof.
explain: Rise is the vertical distance from the horizontal plane of the eaves (wall plate) to the highest point of the ridge.

q: 43. The type of masonry in which the stones of the same height are used and the courses are also of the same height is called ..........
explain: In coursed rubble masonry, stones are roughly squared and laid in distinct horizontal layers (courses).

q: 44. The type of masonry in which the stones are fine chisel dressed and the thickness of joints does not exceed 3 mm is called ..........
explain: Ashlar fine masonry uses perfectly squared, dressed stones with very thin mortar joints for a superior finish.

q: 45. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as ..........
explain: Breast walls protect natural earth slopes from erosion and weathering, whereas retaining walls support man-made fills.

q: 46. The stretcher bond is generally used for ..........
explain: Stretcher bond is only suitable for walls that are half-brick thick (10 cm), like partition walls.

q: 47. The part of a wall at the side of an opening in the masonry is called ..........
explain: Jambs are the vertical sides of an opening for a door or window.

q: 48. Which of the following scaffolding is provided for a building on the side of a busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on road?
explain: Needle scaffolding (or cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' projecting through the wall, leaving the ground clear for traffic.
